full_descriptions: ["HORATIO: Hybrid Online Recognition of Adversary Tactics in Information Ops", "Information operations (IO) operators attend to large volumes of data across regions, timescales, languages, platforms, and adversaries.  Complex AI and machine learning tools can detect indicators of influence but the operator -- who may be a novice in AI, ML, and social science -- is left to integrate results into a model of a complex, coordinated, distributed adversary.  SIFT proposes to develop HORATIO (Hybrid Online Recognition of Adversary Tactics in Information Ops) as a machine teammate for IO analysis.  HORATIO will feature a multimodal (diagram- and dialogue-based) interface for operators to specify IO objectives and workflows, and ", "Information operations (IO) operators attend to large volumes of data across regions, timescales, languages, platforms, and adversaries.  Complex AI and machine learning tools can detect indicators of influence but the operator -- who may be a novice in AI, ML, and social science -- is left to integrate results into a model of a complex, coordinated, distributed adversary.  SIFT proposes to develop HORATIO (Hybrid Online Recognition of Adversary Tactics in Information Ops) as a machine teammate for IO analysis.  HORATIO will feature a multimodal (diagram- and dialogue-based) interface for operators to specify IO objectives and workflows, and then operators will trigger workflows with a playbook-style human-machine interface.  It will use Hierarchical Task Networks (HTNs) to plan and manage these workflows, running a suite of natural language processing (NLP) tools to detect indicators of influence, and then automatically analyzing and accumulating results into a template-like model of red-force tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTP) to contextualize subsequent interactions and analyses with the operator.  This full-loop human-machine operation will bring high-value IO tools into the fold that were previously out-of-reach due to difficultly of operation or complexity of interpretation. To achieve this vision, SIFT will leverage ongoing work on large language models (LLMs), HTNs, NLP, and IO operations. SIFT's recent work fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) -- with low-rank adaptation and constrained decoding -- will help HORATIO read and generate structured data such as workflows, within a mission context.  SIFT is an industry leader in HTN planning and maintains leading open-source HTN planners, and HORATIO will utilize these tools for representing, running, and managing IO workflows.  Finally, SIFT is involved in the DARPA INCAS program, and has produced robust NLP tools for IO analysis -- for detecting topic-based sentiment, emotions, concerns, moral framing, themes, and more -- that will populate HORATIO's initial suite of NLP tools, and more tools are available open-source from other INCAS performers.  Finally, the HORATIO effort will include a consultant on IO narratives, transition partners (see letter of support), and briefings to government operators who are already using SIFT's INCAS technology, all which will prioritize the workflows and TTP that we implement for HORATIO.  SIFT is well-positioned with transition customers in the DoD to build HORATIO and deliver it to operators who need it."]

USE OF WIRE-ARC ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING (WAAM) TO PRODUCE LARGE-SCALE STEEL CASTING REPLACEMENTS OF CASTING ALLOY HY-80 IS OF ONGOING INTEREST TO THE U.S. NAVY. WAAM IS BY FAR THE MOST EFFICIENT ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING (AM) PROCESS TO DEPOSIT MATERIAL AT HIGH RATES COMPARED TO OTHER AM TECHNIQUES. THE HIGH DEPOSITION RATE OF THIS TECHNOLOGY COUPLED WITH THE RELATIVELY INEXPENSIVE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE WAAM TOOLING MAKES THIS PROCESS THE MOST COST EFFECTIVE AM PROCESS FOR STEEL CASTING REPLACEMENTS. DESPITE THE NUMEROUS ADVANTAGES OF WAAM, HOWEVER, THERE IS A SIGNIFICANT UNPREDICTABILITY IN THE RESULTING PERFORMANCE OF THE STEELS PRODUCED BY WAAM. WAAM CURRENTLY RELIES ON COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE FEEDSTOCK MATERIALS AND THESE FEEDSTOCK MATERIALS WERE DESIGNED FOR WELDING, NOT BULK MATERIALS. RECENT WORK FROM ARL/PENN STATE ATTEMPTED PROCESSING WITH MIL-100S-1 FOR CASTING REPLACEMENT USING A LASER BASED DIRECTED ENERGY DEPOSITION (DED) PROCESS. THESE ISSUES MAY BE ADDRESSED BY OPTIMIZING THE STEEL ALLOY FOR WAAM PROCESSING AND BY OPTIMIZING THE POST-PROCESS HEAT TREATING FOR THE WAAM STEEL BUILDS. OPTIMIZING BOTH THE STEELS ALLOYS AND POST-PROCESS HEAT TREATING PROCESSES ARE REQUIRED TO HELP ADDRESS THE CHALLENGES FACING WAAM FOR CASTING REPLACEMENT IN ORDER TO HELP BRING THIS PROCESS AS A VIABLE OPTION FOR REPLACEMENT OF HY-80 CASTINGS FOR THE NAVY.

OBJECTIVE 1: HYPERSPECTRAL UNMIXING IS THE PROCESS OF EXTRACTING UNDERLYING MATERIALS FROM REMOTELY SENSED SPECTROSCOPY, AVAILABLE NATIVELY FROM HSI. IN HSI, AN INDIVIDUAL PIXEL CONTAINS RADIANCE INFORMATION WHICH IS A FUNCTION OF BOTH THE REFLECTIVITY FROM MATERIAL PROPERTIES AS WELL AS ATMOSPHERIC EFFECTS. HYPERSPECTRAL UNMIXING CAN LEVERAGE SIMULATION OR DATA-DRIVEN METHODS. SIMULATION SUCH AS RAY-TRACING USES MONTE CARLO METHODS TO MODEL RANDOM RAY REFLECTION GIVEN AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE CANDIDATE MATERIALS GEOMETRY AND PHYSICAL PROPERTIES. DATA-DRIVEN APPROACHES USE MACHINE LEARNING TO EXTRACT THIS NONLINEAR RELATIONSHIP FROM GROUND TRUTH DATA ITSELF. RAY-TRACING TECHNIQUES LEND THEMSELVES TO SCENARIOS WHERE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES ARE EASILY MODELED, AND DATA-DRIVEN TECHNIQUES ARE EFFECTIVE FOR PROBLEMS WITH CONSIDERABLE GROUND TRUTH DATA. OUR ALGORITHMS ALLOW FOR IMAGING SLOW MOVING TARGETS AND CAN IDENTIFY MOTION FEAURES THAT ARE UNDETECTABLE WHEN USING THE CONVENTIONAL MOTION TARGETS AND CAN IDENTIFY MOTION GEATURES THAT ARE UNDETECTABLE WHEN USING THE CONVENTIONAL MOTION ESTIMATION METHODS. THE USE OF SUCH ILLUMINATION SOURCES HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REDUCE THE COST OF THE INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED FOR SPACE SURVEILLANCE, BUT IT ALSO HAS OTHER ADVANTAGES OVER CONVENTIONAL MATCHED FIELD IMAGING METHODS. ONE SUCH ADVANTAGE IS THAT AT HIGHER FREQUENCIES (K-BAND AND HIGHER), WHICH CAN PROVIDE BETTER RESOLUTION, ATMOSPHERIC INHOMOGENEITIES REQUIRE MITIGATIN. USING CORRELATIONS IS A FIRST STEP IN REDUCING IMAGE BLURRING AND LOCATION UNCERTAINTY. WE HAVE ALSO WORKED ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF SPARSITY CONTRAINT OPTIMIZATION BASED IMAGING METHODS THAT PROVIDE HIGH RESOLUTION IMAGES FROM HIGHLY INCOMPLETE AND NOISY DATA [6]. THIS IS ACHIEVED USING THE NOISE COLLECTOR (NC) TO ABSORB THE NOISE IN THE DATA GUARANTEEING EXACT SUPPORT RECOVERY WHEN THE NOISE IS NOT TOO LARGE AND NO FALSE POSITIVES FOR ANY LEVEL OF NOISE. THE NC WAS RECENTLY USED TO DESIGN A HIGHLY EFFECTIVE DIMENSION REDUCTION ALGORITHM FOR IMAGING WITH CROSS-CORRELATIONS [5]. THIS ALGORITHM PROVIDES HIGH RESOLUTION IMAGES AND MAY BE USED TO IMPROVE UPON THE RESOLUTION OF THE L2 METHODS PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT SATELLITE IMAGING PROBLEM. ALTHOUGH A LOT OF PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE, THERE ARE STILL BASIC RESEARCH ISSUES INVOLVING BOTH NUMERICAL SIMULATIONS AND THEORY THAT NEED TO BE ADDRESSED, ESPECIALLY THOSE THAT INVOLVE THE ROLE OF NOISE AND UNCERTAINTY ABOUT THE AMBIENT MEDIUM, WHICH ARE QUITE CHALLENGING. BASED ON OUR OWN EXPERIENCE WITH NEARLY ALL TYPES OF IMAGING METHODS USED IN THE LAST SEVERAL YEARS WE WANT TO EXPLORE IN DEPTH THE ROLE AND IMPACY OF NN AND ML TECHNIQUES IN IMAGING. PROJECT OVERVIEW
ACTIVE IMAGING OF SMALL SATELLITES WITHIN THE CISLUNAR SPHERE IS CHALLENGING ON MANY FRONTS. THE REQUIRED
OPTICAL RESOLUTION, DETECTOR SENSITIVITY, AND SCANNING/TRACKING PERFORMANCE STRETCHES CURRENT TECHNOLOGY TO
ITS LIMITS, AND MANY IMAGING SCENARIOS ARE CURRENTLY NOT PRACTICAL. WE PROPOSE A RADICALLY NEW OPTICAL
DESIGN THAT ENABLES LARGE ANGLE LASER BEAM STEERING AND FOCUSING OVER SIZABLE OPTICAL APERTURES WITH A
MINIMUM OF MECHANICAL MOTION. COMPARED WITH CONVENTIONAL OPTICAL PHASED ARRAYS, OUR DESIGNS ARE
CAPABLE OF VASTLY LARGER STEERING ANGLES (IN PRINCIPAL, AS LARGE AS 45O), CAN ADDRESS ORDERS-OF-MAGNITUDE
LARGER NUMBERS OF OBJECT POINTS, AND ARE FULLY FOCUSABLE, ALL ACCOMPLISHED BY SMALL DISPLACEMENTS OF LIGHTWEIGHT
FIBERS. IMPORTANTLY, THIS IMAGING MODALITY IS CAPABLE OF ACCESSING AND TRACKING OBJECTS OVER A LARGE
PART OF THE SKY WITH NO MACRO-MOTION. SECOND-ORDER COMPENSATION OF ATMOSPHERIC TURBULENCE CAN ALSO BE
ACHIEVED WITH NO EXTRA HARDWARE, RESULTING IN IMPROVED BEAM QUALITY ON TARGET.
THE OPTICAL SYSTEM WE DESCRIBE IS DESIGNED FOR LASER BEAM FORMING FOR ACTIVE ILLUMINATION OF DISTANT OBJECTS
WITH ULTRA-HIGH RESOLUTION. HOWEVER, THE SAME SYSTEM CAN BE USED IN REVERSE AS THE RECEIVER ELEMENT OF THE
ACTIVE IMAGING SYSTEM, ACTING IN EFFECT AS A LARGE APERTURE, SCANNABLE AND FOCUSABLE IMAGING LASER RADAR.
IT IS THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT TO THOROUGHLY EXPLORE THE DESIGN SPACE OF THE PROPOSED IMAGING MODALITY,
DEVELOP ACCURATE NUMERICAL MODELS TO PREDICT SYSTEM PERFORMANCE, AND DEMONSTRATE CRITICAL HARDWARE
COMPONENTS THROUGH A SERIES OF EVALUATION TESTS AND IMAGING DEMONSTRATIONS.
PROF. LEGER HAS BEEN AWARDED THE 1998 JOSEPH FRAUNHOFER AWARD/ROBERT M. BURLEY PRIZE BY THE OPTICAL
SOCIETY OF AMERICA FOR HIS WORK IN LASER BEAM COMBINING. HE IS A FELLOW OF THE OPTICAL SOCIETY OF AMERICA
(OSA), FELLOW OF THE INSTITUTE OF ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC ENGINEERS (IEEE), AND FELLOW OF THE INTERNATIONAL

BY CREATING AND ANALYZING A RICH KNOWLEDGE BASE OF TEMPORAL ASPECTS IN STRATEGIC THINKING ACROSS MAJOR POWERS, THE PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY PATTERNS, TEST HYPOTHESES, AND GENERATE INSIGHTS THAT CAN INFORM BOTH THEORETICAL UNDERSTANDING AND PRACTICAL POLICY.

THESE APPROACHES WILL BE APPLIED TO A VAST CORPUS OF TEXTUAL AND NUMERICAL DATA RELATED TO US, CHINESE, AND RUSSIAN STRATEGIC POSTURES AND INTERACTIONS.

SELF-LEARNING AS INFERENCE OF NOVEL ABSTRACTIONS

IN THE ROY LAB, WE PROPOSE TO BUILD ON OUR PREVIOUS WORK WHERE WE SHOWED THAT A ROBOT COULD 
INCORPORATE BACKGROUND CONCEPTUAL KNOWLEDGE ENCODED AS A MARKOV LOGIC NETWORK ENCOMPASSING SEMANTIC 
ATTRIBUTES, RELATIONSHIPS, AFFORDANCES ETC. CAN BE USED TO INFER "MISSING" PLAN CONSTITUENTS (SUCH 
AS ACTION SUBJECTS OR GOAL LOCATIONS) BASED ON STATISTICAL CORRELATIONS AND TAXONOMIC AFFINITIES. 
TO REDUCE COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEX-ITY, AN ONLINE CONTEXT-DRIVEN APPROACH CAN BE USED THAT 
HYPOTHESIZES THE POTENTIAL FOR MISSING KNOWLEDGE COMPONENTS BY INTEGRATING EVIDENCE FROM THE VISUAL 
OBSERVATIONS OF THE WORLD STATE. THE ABILITY TO INFER LATENT PLAN COMPONENTS ENABLES THE ROBOT TO 
TAKE INFORMATION GATHERING ACTIONS SUCH AS VISUAL EXPLORATION OR ENGAGING IN DIALOGUE WITH THE 
HUMAN TO REPLENISH ITS KNOWLEDGE GAP AND ENABLE PLAN SYNTHESIS.

PROBLEMS THAT ARE LONG-HORIZON AND HIGH DIMENSIONAL ARE USUALLY INTRACTABLE FOR END-TO-END LEARNING 
PRO-CESSES. THE STRATEGY IS TO RENDER THESE PROBLEMS TRACTABLE BY EXPLOITING STRUCTURE IN THE 
PROBLEM, INCLUDING FACTORING INTO WEAKLY INTERACTING SUB-COMPONENTS (POSSIBLY INVOLVING DIFFERENT 
ASPECTS OF THE STATE SPACE OR DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SUB-REGIONS), AND "LIFTING" OR ABSTRACTING OVER 
ARBITRARY SETS OF ENTITIES IN THE DOMAIN. THE REPRESENTATIONS THAT HAVE EFFECTIVELY ENABLED 
COMPACTNESS AND EFFICIENT REASONING IN VERY LARGE PROBLEMS ARE LOGICS, INCLUDING PROPOSITIONAL 
LOGIC, FIRST-ORDER LOGIC, GRAPHICAL MODELS (WHICH CAN BE VIEWED AS A PROBA-BILISTIC VERSION OF 
PROPOSITIONAL LOGIC) AND TEMPORAL LOGICS. THE PRIMARY VIRTUE OF LOGICAL REPRESENTATIONS IS THAT 
THEY ALLOW COMPOSITIONALITY -  A LOGICAL REPRESENTATION PROVIDES A SYSTEM OF RULES THAT ALLOW 
SYNTACTIC MANIPULATIONS TO CREATE NEW REPRESENTATIONS WHILE PRESERVING THE SEMANTICS OF THE MODEL. 
CONCRETELY, PARTS OF THE MODEL CAN HAVE INDEPENDENT SEMANTICS, ALLOWING THEM TO BE LEARNED 
INDEPENDENTLY AND THEN COMPOSED USING LOGICAL OPERATIONS TO INFER THE SEMANTICS OF A COMBINED 
MODEL, PROVIDING A PARTICULARLY AGGRESSIVE AND USEFUL FORM OF GENERALIZATION.

MODELING UNCERTAINTY

A CRUCIAL ABILITY FOR LONG-TERM AUTONOMY IS THE ABILITY TO INTROSPECT, AND RECOGNISE WHEN ITS 
INTERNAL MODEL IS ACCURATE AND WHEN IT IS UNCERTAIN. IT IS IMPORTANT TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN TWO 
TYPES OF UNCERTAINTY: ALEATORIC UNCERTAINTY THAT CAPTURES STOCHASTICITY IN SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND 
THE ENVIRONMENT, AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY THAT RESULTS FROM AN INCOMPLETE MODEL OF THE WORLD. HIGH 
ALEATORIC UNCERTAINTY IMPLIES THAT EXPECTED RISK CAN BE CALCULATED ACCURATELY, WHEREAS EPISTEMIC 
UNCERTAINTY MEANS THAT THERE ARE PARTS OF THE SENSOR DATA THAT THE VEHICLE CANNOT ACCURATELY MODEL. 
SEPARATING ALEATORIC AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY ALLOWS FOR A PROCESS OF MODIFYING RISK PROFILES WHEN 
NO FEASIBLE PLAN IS FOUND, POTENTIALLY INCREASING THE TOLERANCE FOR RISK DUE TO ALEATORIC 
UNCERTAINTY UNTIL A FEASIBLE PLAN IS FOUND.

WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE OUR PREVIOUS WORK IN ANOMALY DETECTION (ALSO REFERRED TO AS 
OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION OR OOD DETECTION). IN NOVEL ENVIRONMENTS, UNCERTAINTY ESTIMATES CAN BE 
DIFFICULT TO CALIBRATE AND, AS A RESULT, OOD REJECTION CAN BE USED TO REPLACE OR IMPROVE UPON 
EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY ESTIMATES AS A WAY TO REDUCE THE IMPACT OF ERRONEOUS OUTPUTS FROM 
'UNEXPECTED' SENSOR DATA. OUR PAST WORK HAS INVESTIGATED ANOMALY 
DETECTION VIA AUTOENCODERS AND VIA LEARNED REPRESENTATIONS OF BELIEF. LEVERAGING OUR EXPERIENCE 
WITH BOTH OOD REJECTION AND DEEP MODELS OF ALEATORIC AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY, WE PROPOSE TO 
INVESTIGATE SEVERAL AVENUES OF UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION IN AN EFFORT TO DETERMINE A ROBUST 
APPROACH FOR SEMANTIC PERCEPTION.

["AWD-004814-S1", "CHEMICAL IMPULSE ACTUATION FOR AERODYNAMIC FLOW CONTROL", "IF AWARDED BY OFFICE OF NAVAL RESEARCH, VPI IS PREPARED TO SUPPORT THE GEORGIA TECH EFFORT PERFORMING THE FOLLOWING TASKS:
1.	PROPELLANT CHARACTERIZATION
IN THIS TASK VPI WILL IDENTIFY PROPELLANT CHEMISTRIES SUITABLE FOR CHEMICAL IMPULSE ACTUATION CONSIDERING ENERGY, ENERGY DENSITY, RESPONSE CHARACTERISTICS, AND OPERABILITY. DURING THIS TASK PROPELLANT CLASSES AND CHEMISTRIES UNDER CONSIDERATION INCLUDE LIQUID/GEL MONOPROPELLANTS, LIQUID OR HYBRID HYPERGOLIC PROPELLANTS, AND SOLID PROPELLANTS.
OPERABILITY CONSIDERATIONS INCLUDE VARIABLES SUCH AS THE ABILITY TO BE DELIVERED OVER A RANGE OF OPERATING SCALES (VISCOSITY FOR LIQUIDS AND GELS), RES", "IF AWARDED BY OFFICE OF NAVAL RESEARCH, VPI IS PREPARED TO SUPPORT THE GEORGIA TECH EFFORT PERFORMING THE FOLLOWING TASKS:
1.	PROPELLANT CHARACTERIZATION
IN THIS TASK VPI WILL IDENTIFY PROPELLANT CHEMISTRIES SUITABLE FOR CHEMICAL IMPULSE ACTUATION CONSIDERING ENERGY, ENERGY DENSITY, RESPONSE CHARACTERISTICS, AND OPERABILITY. DURING THIS TASK PROPELLANT CLASSES AND CHEMISTRIES UNDER CONSIDERATION INCLUDE LIQUID/GEL MONOPROPELLANTS, LIQUID OR HYBRID HYPERGOLIC PROPELLANTS, AND SOLID PROPELLANTS.
OPERABILITY CONSIDERATIONS INCLUDE VARIABLES SUCH AS THE ABILITY TO BE DELIVERED OVER A RANGE OF OPERATING SCALES (VISCOSITY FOR LIQUIDS AND GELS), RESPONSE BEHAVIOR CONSIDERING OFF AMBIENT TEMPERATURE CONDITIONS (BOTH HOT AND COLD). PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF PROPELLANTS SUCH AS DENSITY, VISCOSITY, AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES WILL MEASURED AS APPROPRIATE. ALL PROPELLANTS UNDER CONSIDERATION WILL BE SUBJECT TO THERMAL CHARACTERIZATION VIA TGA/DSC. 
RESPONSE TIME, OR IGNITION DELAY, WILL BE CHARACTERIZED AS A FUNCTION OF INPUT STIMULI (AS NECESSARY), SCALE, AND INITIAL TEMPERATURE. THROUGH THE USE OF REACTIVE/CATALYTIC, OR OTHER MECHANISM ALTERING ADDITIVE, RESPONSE TIMES WILL BE OPTIMIZED. IF PROPELLANTS REQUIRE A CATALYST OR ELECTRICAL INPUT TO INITIATE, THE POWER REQUIREMENTS WILL BE FULLY DETERMINED. FOR MONOPROPELLANTS AND SOLID PROPELLANTS, THEIR COMBUSTION BEHAVIOR, NAMELY BURNING RATE, WILL BE MEASURED AS A FUNCTION OF PRESSURE IN A STRAND BURNING CONFIGURATION. AS APPROPRIATE, THE QUENCHING CHARACTERISTICS OF THE PROPELLANTS WILL BE DETERMINED AS A FUNCTION OF PRESSURE.      
2.	BENCHTOP ACTUATOR CHARACTERIZATION 
VPI IN COORDINATION WITH GT WILL DESIGN AND FABRICATE REACTION CHAMBERS TO ENABLE IMPULSE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE MOST PROMISING CHEMISTRIES IDENTIFIED IN TASK 1. VPI WILL DETERMINE OPTIMUM OPERATIONAL LIMITS FOR THE REACTION CHAMBERS VIA MEASUREMENTS OF PRESSURE AND THRUST. IN ADDITION, PLUME TEMPERATURE MEASUREMENTS WILL BE MADE USING PYROMETRIC TECHNIQUES. INITIALLY A REACTION CHAMBER WILL BE CHARACTERIZED WITH A SINGLE PULSE OF VARYING DURATIONS. THIS WILL BE FOLLOWED BY A SINGLE REACTION CHAMBER FIRING REPETITIVELY.  ONE QUESTION TO BE ADDRESSED IS THE FREQUENCY AT WHICH A CHAMBER MAY BE FIRED FOR A GIVEN PROPELLANT CHEMISTRY. THE LAST PORTION OF THIS TASK IS THE DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION OF AN ARRAY OF REACTION CHAMBERS WHICH WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED IN COORDINATION WITH GT. ALONG WITH THE REACTION CHAMBER ITSELF, THE PROPELLANT DELIVERY SYSTEM WILL BE CHARACTERIZED IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND THE FREQUENCY AND RESPONSIVENESS OF THE ENTIRE SYSTEM.
3.	INTERACTIONS OF IMPULSE ACTUATION WITH A CROSS FLOW
VPI WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO GT FOR EXPERIMENTS INVOLVING ACTUATION WITH A CROSS FLOW. THIS MAY INCLUDE EITHER SUPPLYING APPROPRIATE PROPELLANTS OR TRANSFERRING THE INFORMATION REQUIRED FOR FORMULATION. VPI PERSONNEL WILL TRAVEL TO GT TO SUPPORT EXPERIMENTS AT THE REQUEST OF GT.
4.	LARGE-SCALE SEPARATION CONTROL 
VPI WILL COORDINATE IN THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF A FULL CHEMICAL IMPULSE ACTUATION SYSTEM FOR EXPERIMENTATION IN A HIGH-SPEED WIND TUNNEL ON AN AERODYNAMIC MODEL. EXPERIMENTATION IS PROPOSED TO OCCUR IN THE AIR FORCE ACADEMY SUBSONIC WIND TUNNEL. VPI WILL SUPPORT ON SITE EXPERIMENTATION.

5.	PROJECT REPORTING
VPI WILL COORDINATE WITH GT AND DELIVER ALL NECESSARY DOCUMENTATION FOR REPORTING TO ONR FOR MID AND END YEAR REPORTING AS REQUIRED BY ONR.  IN ADDITION, VPI WILL SUPPORT PROGRAM SPECIFIC ANNUAL MEETINGS WITH GT AND ONR, AS WELL AS ONR PROGRAM REVIEW MEETINGS."]

STRESS, AS NAVY OPERATIONS OFTEN REQUIRE SAILORS TO PERFORM COMPLEX TASKS IN THESE PHYSIOLOGICAL
STATES. WE WILL ALSO TEST INTERVENTIONS DESIGNED TO REMEDIATE DEFICITS DUE TO SLEEP DEPRIVATION AND
EXAMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH TRAINING CAN INOCULATE INDIVIDUALS AGAINST THE DELETERIOUS EFFECTS OF
SLEEP DEPRIVATION ON NAVY-RELEVANT PERFORMANCE.
THE SPECIFIC AIM OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO TEST WHETHER SLEEP DEPRIVATION AND STRESS REDUCE
ATTENTION CONTROL, AND WHETHER EFFECTS OF THESE STRESSORS ARE SIMILAR FOR COMPONENTS OF ATTENTION
CONTROL SUCH AS SUSTAINED ATTENTION AND VIGILANCE. THE WORK WILL ALSO TEST WHETHER INTERVENTIONS
SUCH AS CAFFEINE, EXPOSURE TO BLUE-WAVELENGTH LIGHT WILL COMBAT PERFORMANCE DEFICITS IN ATTENTION
CONTROL DUE TO SLEEP DEPRIVATION, AND WHETHER EXTENSIVE TRAINING IN A TASK CAN CREATE AN IMMUNITY
TO SLEEP DEPRIVATION AND REDUCE DEFICITS DUE TO SLEEP DEPRIVATION.
WE WILL ADDRESS THESE AIMS IN FIVE EXPERIMENTS. IN THE FIRST TWO EXPERIMENTS, WE WILL
INVESTIGATE MODULATIONS IN ATTENTION CONTROL DUE TO PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES COMMON IN NAVY
OPERATIONS, SLEEP DEPRIVATION AND STRESS. IN THE SECOND TWO EXPERIMENTS, WE WILL EVALUATE
INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE THE IMPACT OF SLEEP DEPRIVATION ON ATTENTION CONTROL. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL
ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF CAFFEINE AND BLUE-ENRICHED LIGHT. FINALLY, IN THE LAST EXPERIMENT, WE WILL

PROBLEM STATEMENT
CHARGE NOISE IS A KEY FACTOR LIMITING THE PERFORMANCE OF SPIN QUBITS IN SEMICONDUCTOR QUANTUM DOTS. MITIGATING CHARGE NOISE REQUIRES A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF ITS ORIGINS AND STATISTICAL PROPERTIES. EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT CHARGE NOISE ORIGINATES IN THE SURFACE OF THE SEMICONDUCTOR DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF PARTICLES WITH DIPOLE MOMENTS, KNOWN AS TWO-LEVEL FLUCTUATORS (TLFS). HOWEVER, LITTLE IS KNOWN REGARDING THE DENSITY OF THE TLFS OR THE MAGNITUDES AND ORIENTATIONS OF THEIR ELECTRIC
DIPOLE MOMENTS. THE DENSITY, IN PARTICULAR, IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A CRITICAL ROLE IN DETERMINING THE
STATISTICS OF CHARGE NOISE. WHEN THE DENSITY IS LARGE AND A QUBIT INTERACTS WITH MANY TLFS, THE CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM IMPLIES THAT CHARGE NOISE IS GAUSSIAN DISTRIBUTED. ON THE OTHER HAND, WHEN THE CONCENTRATION IS SPARSE AND A QUBIT INTERACTS STRONGLY WITH ONLY A FEW TLFS, THE CHARGE NOISE
SHOULD DISPLAY NON-GAUSSIAN STATISTICS. WITH FEW EXCEPTIONS, EXISTING WORK ON SPIN QUBITS TREATS CHARGE NOISE AS GAUSSIAN, EVEN THOUGH
EXPERIMENTAL FINDINGS INDICATE THAT SPIN QUBITS OFTEN INTERACT PREFERENTIALLY WITH A LIMITED NUMBER
OF TLFS. WHILE THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN GAUSSIAN AND NON-GAUSSIAN STATISTICS MAY SEEM ACADEMIC,
NON-GAUSSIAN NOISE ALTERS THE SPECTRAL RESPONSE OF QUANTUM SYSTEMS TO CONTROL AND CONVENTIONAL
ERROR MITIGATION TECHNIQUES SUCH AS DYNAMICAL DECOUPLING. ADDRESSING CHARGE NOISE IN SPIN QUBITS
REQUIRES AN APPROACH TO DETECT, CHARACTERIZE AND MODEL NON-GAUSSIAN EFFECTS. THIS WILL ENABLE THE
DESIGN OF ERROR MITIGATION, GATES AND CONTROL, ROBUST TO THE UNIQUE DYNAMICAL EFFECTS OF NON-GAUSSIAN CHARGE NOISE.
PROJECT GOALS
APL WILL DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO DETECT, CHARACTERIZE AND MITIGATE NON-GAUSSIAN CHARGE NOISE USING
NON-GAUSSIAN ARMA MODELS.

1. YEAR 1:
A. DEVELOP A MULTI-AXIS NOISE MODEL FOR A SINGLET-TRIPLET SPIN QUBIT THAT ACCOUNTS FOR QUASI-STATIC HYPERFINE NOISE AND CHARGE NOISE, TREATED AN AUTOREGRESSIVE-MOVING-AVERAGE (ARMA) MODEL.
B. USE NOISE MODEL TO DESIGN A TEST ON EXPERIMENTAL DATA THAT DETERMINES WHETHER NON-GAUSSIAN EFFECTS ARE DYNAMICALLY SIGNIFICANT.
2. YEAR 2:
A. DEVISE APPROACH TO EXPERIMENTALLY CHARACTERIZE NON-GAUSSIAN CHARGE NOISE BY FITTING THE COEFFICIENTS OF A NON-GAUSSIAN ARMA MODEL TO MEASURED DATA.
B. PROVIDE SUPPORT TO THE EXPERIMENTAL TEAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ROCHESTER TO IMPLEMENT NON-GAUSSIAN CHARGE NOISE CHARACTERIZATION ON A SINGLET-TRIPLET QUBIT.
3. YEAR 3:
A. USING NOISE MODEL COMBINED WITH NUMERICAL OPTIMAL CONTROL AND/OR ANALYTIC TECHNIQUES,
DETERMINE OPEN-LOOP CONTROL THAT MAXIMIZES THE FIDELITY OF A QUBIT SUBJECT TO NON-GAUSSIAN NOISE.
B. COMPARE WITH EXISTING OPEN-LOOP ERROR SUPPRESSION TECHNIQUES.
4. YEAR 4:
A. APPLY THE IN SITU VALLEY NOISE PROBE TECHNIQUE DEVELOPED BY UMBC TO DESIGN AN APPROACH FOR DYNAMICALLY UPDATING THE NON-GAUSSIAN NOISE MODEL WHILE A QUBIT IS IN OPERATION.
B. ESTABLISH ADAPTIVE CONTROL PROTOCOL IN WHICH THE MOST CURRENT VERSION OF NOISE MODEL IS FED FORWARD TO DYNAMICALLY UPDATE THE CONTROL STRATEGY ESTABLISHED IN YEAR 3.

["179919770", "RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CONTRACTS", "THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT (UCONN), RTX TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH CENTER (RTRC) AND RAYTHEON (LEGACY RAYTHEON MISSILES AND DEFENSE (RMD)) PROPOSE THE MANUFACTURING RESEARCH FOR HYPERSONIC AIR-BREATHING WEAPONS (MRPHAW) PROGRAM, A 47-MONTH EFFORT TO INCREASE THE MANUFACTURING READINESS OF ADVANCED AIRFRAME WELDMENTS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS AND MATERIAL UNDERSTANDING FOR NICKEL-BASED ALLOYS (E.G., INCONEL 718 AND 625, HAYNES 230 AND 282).
MRPHAW WILL DEVELOP, PROTOTYPE AND TRANSITION LEADING-EDGE RESEARCH TO ADDRESS HISTORICAL CHALLENGES IN: (I) ELECTRON-BEAM WELD MODELING; (II) CRACKING IN AND AROUND WELDMENTS; AND, (III) MATERIAL SOURCI", "THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT (UCONN), RTX TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH CENTER (RTRC) AND RAYTHEON (LEGACY RAYTHEON MISSILES AND DEFENSE (RMD)) PROPOSE THE MANUFACTURING RESEARCH FOR HYPERSONIC AIR-BREATHING WEAPONS (MRPHAW) PROGRAM, A 47-MONTH EFFORT TO INCREASE THE MANUFACTURING READINESS OF ADVANCED AIRFRAME WELDMENTS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS AND MATERIAL UNDERSTANDING FOR NICKEL-BASED ALLOYS (E.G., INCONEL 718 AND 625, HAYNES 230 AND 282).
MRPHAW WILL DEVELOP, PROTOTYPE AND TRANSITION LEADING-EDGE RESEARCH TO ADDRESS HISTORICAL CHALLENGES IN: (I) ELECTRON-BEAM WELD MODELING; (II) CRACKING IN AND AROUND WELDMENTS; AND, (III) MATERIAL SOURCING-DRIVEN WELD VARIATIONS. MRPHAW WILL DEVELOP WELD PARAMETER AND HEAT TREAT SOLUTIONS FOR AM TO WROUGHT JOINTS TO PREVENT WELD CRACKING AND HAVE HIGHER FIDELITY ANALYSIS FOR NEW DESIGNS.

OBJECTIVES - NEW RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING IN: (A) THE CHARACTERISTICS, BEHAVIORS AND MODELING OF DISSIMILAR ALLOY WELDS; (B) THE PREDICTION AND MITIGATION OF HOT CRACKING, DISTORTION, AND RESIDUAL STRESSES; AND, (C) THE IMPACTS OF SOURCE MATERIAL VARIATIONS WELDED COMPONENTS. MRPHAW ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES BY THROUGH FOUR MAIN THRUSTS: (I) WELD PROCESS MAPPING TO GAIN UNDERSTANDING OF HIGH NICKEL ALLOY WELD CHARACTERISTICS; ; (II) WELD STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE DISTORTIONS; (III) PREDICTION AND MITIGATION OF HOT CRACKING; AND, (IV) RESEARCH TO PREDICT AND MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF SOURCE MATERIAL VARIATIONS ON WELD CHARACTERISTICS.

SCOPE OF WORK - RTX WILL SUPPORT MRPHAW EXECUTION ACROSS FIVE TASKS. THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE IS FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2023 TO AUGUST 20, 2027 (47 MONTHS).

TASK 1: WELD PROCESS MAPPING - THIS TASK SHALL FOCUS ON COMBINATIONS OF NI-BASED ALLOYS TO INCLUDE INCO 625, INCO 718, HAYNES 230 AND HAYNES 282.
- RTRC SHALL PROVIDE PERMUTATIONS OF MATERIAL COMBINATIONS, WELD METHOD & PARAMETERS, JOINT
CONFIGURATIONS, & PLATE THICKNESSES MOST RELEVANT TO CRACKING ISSUES.
- RTRC SHALL FACILITATE JOINING OPERATIONS BY PROVIDING WELDED SAMPLES AND ACCOMPANYING WELD
PARAMETER DATA THAT BRACKET ACTUAL AEROSTRUCTURE ASSEMBLY PROCESSES.

THIS WILL BE DONE BY ADDING A RANDOM PERTURBATION TO IT. Testbeds, like the ESnet testbed, are commonly used to evaluate and optimize network performance, but physical testbeds have inherent limitations in scalability, cost, and flexibility. A network digital twin, a virtual replica of a physical network, provides a powerful tool to overcome these limitations. It enables experimentation at scale, exploration of ”what-if” scenarios, and long-term simulations that would be difficult or impossible with physical testbeds alone. Network simulators have been widely used in network research and are well-suited for integration into a network digital twin. However, these tools are typically slow in rapid research and development environments, as even simulating a millisecond of network traffic can take hours when maintaining high fidelity. To address this, we propose developing a digital twin framework that guides users through the entire network simulation workflow. The tool will integrate several network simulators, each focusing on different aspects of network behavior, such as hardware and network protocols, to provide a comprehensive understanding of complex network infrastructures. To accelerate simulation, we will employ a hybrid modeling approach, combining high-fidelity simulation with machine learning models that can “fast-forward” through parts of the simulation. In Phase I, a prototype of the digital twin framework and an interactive visualization dashboard was developed to help users understand simulation results. Additionally, an initial machine learning model was created to predict switch behavior of the ESnet testbed. In Phase II, the framework will be expanded to include a user-friendly application that guides users through the process of configuring models, network topologies, simulation ensembles, and visualizing results. Machine learning models will also be enhanced to further speed up simulations, with the integration of foundation models and federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy. After Phase II, the framework will be expanded beyond research network providers, such as the DOE, to support cloud service providers, which manage applications requiring high throughput and low latency. These applications, such as streaming analytics services, are used for real-time decision making, where increased latency can result in financial consequences for users of cloud services. The proposed framework has the potential to improve the design and operation of these systems by providing insights into network performance optimization, planning, and resource management."]

While analytical tools, enabled through modeling and simulation (M&S), exist to support this process, they are still far too heavyweight—limiting the number and quality of options explored and developed. To ensure future dominance, the decision cycle for course of action (COA) development must be radically condensed. COA development involves two critical elements: COA planning and COA adjudication Currently, digital tools for COA planning and adjudication are produced as stovepipes; that is, monolithic applications that are tightly coupled and not easily separable or composable with other applications. As a result, unlocking the full potential of COA planning will continue to be restrained without advances in COA adjudication. Modern M&S tools are ideal candidates for effective COA adjudication However, high-fidelity simulations remain prohibitively expensive for COA adjudication. To address these constraints, researchers have explored simulation acceleration techniques, broadly categorized as reduced order models (ROMs). ROMs aim to preserve key behaviors of complex simulations while drastically reducing computational cost. What is needed is to accelerate COA adjudication using customized ROMs that reflect the real world at an appropriate level of fidelity and that can be executed more rapidly than current high-fidelity simulations or manual analyses. To achieve this, several challenges must be overcome. ROMs typically lose expressivity, failing to capture the full richness of original system representations. What is needed is representation that is expressive enough to fully capture the complex native data structures while enabling the learning of ROMs for system dynamics. Second, current ROM approaches bundle together entity dynamics, forcing the ROM to slow down to the “weakest link.” A method is needed to extract features describing entity dynamics while explicitly modeling the interaction structure and separability. Third, these ROMs must predict dynamics across heterogeneous, adaptive timescales to support rapid application-dependent adjudication. To address these challenges, we are pleased to introduce Neural Network Enhancements for Customized Reduced Order Models to Accelerate Nuanced COA Evaluation and Reasoning (NECROMANCER). NECROMANCER proposes a novel neural network architecture and learning paradigm to learn expressive, separable, and accelerated ROMs. NECROMANCER combines a grammar-structured autoencoder, a transformer-based entity interaction model, and an entity-structured dynamics model featuring black-box deep neural network regression and Koopman mode estimation to produce customized ROMs that can accelerate COA adjudication."]

However, even with the best sensors and training, pilots can only react to terrain and obstacles they are cognitively aware of. Pilots are currently limited to what they can see (including with sensors) or know from a map and hazards overlays, but such tools do not have detailed knowledge of the conflict area. This means that in unfamiliar locations, even the best pilots cannot replicate the performance they can achieve when flying in well-understood areas. What is needed is a cognitive terrain flight assistant (CTFA), to provide the pilot with improved awareness of the terrain and obstacles. To build such a system using machine learning algorithms requires addressing three distinct challenges. First, we must capture terrain data at a suitable level of fidelity. We must have access to a digital twin of the combat space at the correct level of fidelity. Second, we must be able to rapidly reason about candidate flight and path options. This planning function must consider the full set of possible options and be sensitive to the capabilities of the specific aircraft and its mission, as well as the terrain and obstacles. This requires a simulation environment that encodes all of these features. Third, we must be able to develop a CTFA that can understand the impacts of terrain and obstacles on possible flight paths and provide both active (“push”) and requested (“pull”) recommendations to the pilot. Such a capability must be accurately and rapidly learned from the captured terrain data in the simulation environment. Only by addressing all three of these challenges can we produce a CTFA that can successfully help human pilots to achieve their most effective low, close, and fast flight in high-threat environments.
